cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Choose Me
cards.instruction: Make yourself the choice over another person, plan, or obligation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your concert plans may be replaced by my birthday. I've approved an extra slice of cake for you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I bring the friend I bought the tickets with?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your guest is admitted. I will permit both of you to choose your slices first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She only agreed to the concert because I promised her dancing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Dancing is authorized. I'll clear my living room; you may choose the music. Have I approved enough for you to choose me?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 competes with a concert through cake privilege, A3 admits the friend, and A5 authorizes dancing while seeking to be chosen.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 guest question receives A3 approval and preference; B4 dancing commitment causes A5 a room and music concession.

relationship.evidence: B2 protects a friend commitment and B4 explains its substance, giving A a real reason to accommodate both guests.

heightening.evidence: B4 reveals cake is insufficient; A5 broadens the party around dancing and exposes the wish beneath permission-giving.

specificity.evidence: A1 birthday versus concert, B2 purchased tickets and B4 promised dancing establish understandable competing plans.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 asking whether enough has been approved makes the hidden need visible through the same high-status vocabulary.
